subject.title: /learn's skill-authoring-and-apply pipeline has no owner gate, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path

question: Should Skill Workshop lifecycle writes require owner-tier authorization at the `/learn` entry point, the dynamic tool/service mutation path, the `/approve` resolution path, or all of those layers?
rationale: The bug is concrete, but the durable boundary must be chosen by maintainers because callers can reach Skill Workshop lifecycle mutation through command routing, dynamic tool execution, and approval resolution separately.

options.title: Enforce owner at every mutation boundary
options.body: Require owner-tier authorization before `/learn` can start Skill Workshop authoring, before lifecycle apply/reject/quarantine can execute, and before `/approve` can resolve those lifecycle approvals.

options.title: Gate only chat entry points
options.body: Block non-owner `/learn` and `/approve` while leaving lower-level tool/service calls governed by existing approval policy, which is smaller but trusts every non-chat caller.

options.title: Fold into broader approval-evidence design
options.body: Treat this as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93278, accepting that the concrete bypass remains unresolved until the larger approval model is settled.

recommendation.title: Enforce owner at every mutation boundary
recommendation.body: Require owner-tier authorization before `/learn` can start Skill Workshop authoring, before lifecycle apply/reject/quarantine can execute, and before `/approve` can resolve those lifecycle approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current `/learn` command and the recent Skill Workshop lifecycle approval changes, which are the central decision surfaces.
